title: Ukrainian Borscht
description: Beet soup with a beef broth base, soured with vinegar at the end so the colour stays red rather than turning brown. Makes a large pot and improves for three days.
notes: The vinegar is not for flavour alone — acid is what fixes the pigment. Add it too late and the pot has already gone dull.

steps.text: Simmer the beef short rib in the water, skimming the foam off for the first few minutes, until the meat is tender.
steps.tip: Skim properly at the start and the broth stays clear for the rest of the cook.

steps.text: Lift out the beef, pull the meat from the bone, and return it to the pot.
Fry the onion and carrots until soft, then add the beets, tomato paste, and one tablespoon of the red wine vinegar and cook down.
steps.tip: Souring the beets in the pan is the insurance policy for the colour.

steps.text: Add the potatoes to the broth and cook until nearly done.
Stir in the beet mixture and the white cabbage and simmer until the cabbage is just tender.
Off the heat, stir in the crushed garlic and the remaining vinegar, then season hard.
Serve with dill and a spoonful of sour cream in each bowl.
